conviction_note: Q3 is guided as the seasonally weakest quarter, and the 2-estimate consensus ($57.43M / $0.24) sits inside what the guide implies. The company has beaten and raised twice this year, but the name faded its Q2 beat (intraday +10%, close +0.56%), trades above every sell-side target and carries 9.4% short interest. The findings sum to +0.45 and the scaled number is +0.2 (p_up 52 x abs 5.0); both are near zero and agree in sign.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus revenue $57.43M, EPS $0.24 (range $0.17-0.29, 2 estimates; Sidoti cut to $0.17 on 2026-08-05), https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/onespan-nasdaqospn-hits-new-52-week-high-following-better-than-expected-earnings-2026-08-05/ and https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/sidoti-has-negative-estimate-for-onespan-q3-earnings-2026-08-12/. Cross-check against the company guide (FY rev $248-252M, S&S $202-204M, HW $46-48M, adj. EBITDA $67-71M; H1 actual rev $126.4M, HW $22.0M, EBITDA $37.9M; CFO said about 1/3 of H2 hardware falls in Q3 and Q3 is the seasonal low): the guide implies Q3 revenue of about $56.3-57.9M, so the 2-estimate bar sits inside it. FY consensus EPS $1.05-1.09. Only two estimates, so sizes on the reported-quarter line are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 3,450,835 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement = 9.4% of 36.85M shares outstanding, 7.76 days to cover. It was 3.62M (5.15 DTC) on 09-30, peaked at 3.96M (10.0 DTC) on 09-15, and was 2.99M on 07-31, so shorts built after the Q2 print and have started covering (https://equibles.com/stocks/ospn/shortinterest, read 2026-10-29). Baseline skew +3.68 vol points (downside paid) and put/call OI 0.17, but the front chain has 234 total OI and a 98%-of-mid ATM spread, so neither the skew nor the ±10.7% implied move on unusualwhales is a usable statement. Spot $19.645 is 4.6% below the 52-week high and 93.6% above the low, +8.9% over 20 days, and above the MarketBeat average target of $17.67 and Rosenblatt's $18. Dimensional filed a passive 13G (5.2%) on 2026-10-08.

findings.finding: Management guided Q3 as the seasonally lowest quarter: about 1/3 of H2 hardware ($8.0-8.7M of the $24-26M H2 implied by the FY $46-48M guide less H1 $22.0M, against Q3'25 hardware of $9.73M) and Digital Agreements overages 'not to the same extent as in Q2'. That puts guide-implied Q3 revenue at about $56.3-57.9M, against a 2-estimate consensus of $57.43M / $0.24 EPS. The company beat consensus revenue by 3.8% and EPS by $0.07 in Q2 on similarly conservative framing, so a small beat inside the guide is the likely print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue $60.47M vs $58.25M consensus, EPS $0.30 vs $0.23, plus a FY raise; intraday +10% to $17.86 but close-to-close +0.56% (baseline), then $15.59 by 2026-08-20. Q1 2026 beat: a reported +3.4% (low-quality templated sources). The baseline median absolute reaction is 1.89% over 4 prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: consensus sits inside the guided seasonal low, so an in-line Q3 is expected. What is not obviously priced is the beat habit. If the market expected another 3-4% beat, the stock would not have faded the last one to +0.56%.
findings.independence: The 8-K figures (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001044777/000104477726000038/ospnex-991q22026.htm, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1044777/000104477725000032/ospnex-991q32025.htm) are the inputs to the arithmetic. They are the same company documents, not independent.

findings.finding: The hardware guide was raised $3M (to $46-48M from $43-45M) on 'increased hardware bookings in the first half of the year as compared to our plan', with about two-thirds of H2 hardware landing in Q4. The CEO said FIDO2 hardware could make 2027 hardware 'flattish rather than declining'. A Q3 call that holds or raises the FY revenue and EBITDA ranges with booked hardware in hand is a third straight raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 raised ARR guidance (reported +3.4%). Q2 2026 raised revenue, hardware and EBITDA guidance: intraday +10%, closed +0.56%. Raises have been sold intraday.
findings.why_not_priced: The bookings remark is public. The stock's +26% since 2026-08-20 ($15.59 to $19.65) suggests some of the H2 visibility is now in the price, which is why this is sized small. If a further raise were fully priced, the stock would not still sit below its 52-week high with shorts at 9.4%.
findings.independence: Same transcript as the ARR finding below. The guidance numbers are in the 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001044777/000104477726000038/ospnex-991q22026.htm). No independent bookings series found.

findings.finding: ARR fell sequentially from $192.1M (Q1, including Build38) to $189.7M (Q2), and NRR slipped from 105% to 103%. An analyst challenged the step-down on the call and management did not answer it directly, citing a previously discussed $3M Cybersecurity headwind and gross retention of about 86% in Cybersecurity. The year-end ARR guide of $194-198M needs +$4.3-8.3M in H2, mostly in Q4 since over half of bookings come after Labor Day, so a flat or down Q3 ARR would reopen the question on the line a subscription-transition stock trades on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history isolating ARR. On Q2 the ARR step-down coincided with the intraday +10% fading to +0.56% close and a further slide to $15.59 by 08-20 (Earnings Whispers shows -7.0% drift after 08-04).
findings.why_not_priced: Both ARR figures are public, but the sequential decline is not in the headline year-on-year +7% that the wire reported. If it were priced, short interest would not have fallen from 3.96M to 3.45M while the stock rose 26% into the print. Sized down because short interest is 9.4%, and that squeeze risk cuts against a negative.
findings.independence: The Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001044777/000104477726000038/ospnex-991q22026.htm) gives the $189.7M and 103%. The call transcript (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-4-onespan-inc-stock/) gives the analyst challenge and the retention figures. These are company documents only.

findings.finding: Short interest is 3.45M shares (9.4% of shares outstanding, 7.76 days to cover) at the 2026-10-15 settlement. It rose from 2.99M on 07-31 to a 3.96M peak on 09-15 and is now being covered as the stock rallied, so a clean beat or raise meets a short base that needs nearly eight days of average volume to exit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. The Q2 squeeze attempt (intraday +10%) did not hold to the close.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public but sits outside the sealed baseline and the option chain is too thin to express it. The 10-15 to 10-30 change is not yet published.

findings.why_not_priced: The run-up is in the baseline, so this is largely priced. What is filed is that the targets have not caught up. If the market believed the targets, the stock would be below $18.

findings.finding: DocuSign, the main e-signature peer, reported after OneSpan last spoke (2026-09-03): revenue $875.7M (+9%) beat a $867M consensus, it raised FY27 revenue guidance and guided Q3 to $886-890M. That points to healthy agreement-workflow demand for OneSpan's Digital Agreements segment (32% of Q2 revenue, +25% y/y). The other 68% is Cybersecurity, which fell 7% y/y and carries the hardware seasonality, so the net effect on OneSpan is small.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history of OSPN reacting to DocuSign prints found.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a proxy, and OneSpan management already said H2 overages will be much lower than H1, so the Digital Agreements line is partly guided down. It is filed small as a peer read-through, not a company number.
findings.independence: This is a proxy and the only peer source. Company-confirmed Digital Agreements growth (+25% in Q2) is in https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001044777/000104477726000038/ospnex-991q22026.htm.

findings.finding: Cash fell from $70.5M (2025-12-31) to $43.3M (2026-06-30), with a $5.0M draw on the $100M MUFG revolver. The money went to Build38 ($34.6M), buybacks ($8.3M year to date, $47.1M left on the May 2026 authorisation) and the $0.13 quarterly dividend. That is a known use of funds, not distress, but it limits how much buyback can be announced alongside the print.
findings.why_not_priced: The figures are in the 10-Q and the revolver draw is not in the wire copy. It is sized at zero because the money buys an acquisition and capital returns that are already visible.
findings.independence: The 8-K balance sheet (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001044777/000104477726000038/ospnex-991q22026.htm) is the same company document.

findings.finding: DigipassONE, the unified authentication platform built on the Nok Nok and Build38 acquisitions, is in customer POCs in H2 2026. The CEO said 'the impact's more in 2027 than in 2026 in terms of tangible revenue', so the Q3 call can add narrative but not numbers.
findings.why_not_priced: Product commentary with no revenue attached. It would only move the stock if a named bank win or a 2027 framing were given on the call.
findings.independence: The Q2 8-K CEO quote on DigipassONE and agentic use cases: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001044777/000104477726000038/ospnex-991q22026.htm

outside_window.finding: FY2027 guidance (including whether hardware turns flat on FIDO2 and DigipassONE revenue) is not given until the Q4 print in February 2027. Management said 'we're not giving guidance for next year'.

baseline_tension: Mixed. The modest downside skew (from an unusable chain), the run-up to above every target and Q2's faded beat argue against the long lean from the beat-and-raise habit and 9.4% short interest. Both sides are small, so p_up sits at 52.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar has two estimates and lands inside the guided Q3 low): reported-quarter beat finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3.
Lesson 1 (this name sold its Q2 beat and raise, +10% intraday to +0.56% close): guidance finding cut from +0.8 to +0.6; p_up held at 52 rather than higher.
Lesson 7 (short interest 9.4%, 7.8 days to cover): negatives shrunk, ARR from -1.0 to -0.8 and above-targets from -0.7 to -0.4.
Lesson 9 (segment proxy): DocuSign read-through cut from +0.2 to +0.15, net of the 68% Cybersecurity side.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the revolver draw funds Build38 and returns, so it stays at 0.
Lesson 5's line that positioning 'does not file' was not applied to remove findings, because the shared core's four drop reasons govern; the positioning findings were kept small instead.
